prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on the balance sheet: profit covers interest costs 11.8 times over. Also in its favour: debt is lower than shareholders' equity (debt-to-equity 0.39); return on capital employed is 16.7%, a strong return on the money in the business; and profit grew 33.0% a year on average over three years. Other areas on this side: cash flow and the balance sheet, what the price asks for the earnings, growth.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on the recent price trend: momentum scores only 11 of 100 against the comparison pool. Also against it: the share price is 31.5% lower than a year ago; over the past year the share did 29.8 percentage points worse than the Nifty 50; and the share price is 34% below its 52-week high. Other areas on this side: growth, price behaviour, the quality of the business.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 6 points in favour and 12 against give more points against. The pool score is 40 of 100. The side that carries most weight is the recent price trend. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
